reason: Re-opened al-Tabari via packet.js quran 46 --verse 33.21: the comment covers 33:21 to 33:22 as one segment, and after the note on the readings of uswa he says in his own voice that the ayah is a reproach from God to the believers who stayed behind from the Messenger and his camp at Medina, that they should model themselves on him and be with him wherever he was, and that whoever hopes for God's reward and mercy does not hold his own life dearer (la yarghabu bi-nafsihi) but is with him wherever he is. The evidence words are verbatim at that place and carry the whole paraphrase (reproach to those who hung back; not sparing himself; being with him wherever he is) without drift; this is his own statement, not only the Ibn Ishaq report that follows. Locator right (one comment on 33:21 to 33:22). verse.js ok (Al-Ahzab 33:21, at 3553); entry-check ok. Plain sense checked against day.js: the clans come upon the believers from above and below (33:9 to 33:10, 33:20, 33:22) and some seek the Prophet's permission to leave (33:13); 'lay siege' and 'waverers' are light glosses of the passage's own terms (the text calls the leave-seekers a party of the hypocrites and those with disease in their hearts who wished to flee), not a material softening; no school, comparison or other tradition; tone plain. Attacks tried on every line and none landed.
